identification.summary: UAC-0194 is a CERT-UA tracking designation for a threat cluster believed to be linked to Russia, tied to a phishing campaign that exploited the Windows NTLM hash-disclosure zero-day CVE-2024-43451 against Ukrainian targets [S2][S7]. ClearSky reported the exploitation, and CERT-UA attributed distribution of the malicious URL files to UAC-0194 [S2]. The chain delivered a ZIP containing a .URL shortcut that, on right-click, delete or drag, contacted a remote server to fetch further payloads including the open-source SparkRAT, and attempted NTLM hash capture over SMB [S2][S3][S5].
identification.firstObserved: ClearSky reported CVE-2024-43451 exploitation since at least April 2024 [S3]. Public CERT-UA/ClearSky-linked reporting dates to November 2024 [S2].
identification.notes: UAC-0194 is a CERT-UA 'UAC' uncategorized-cluster number, not a vendor-assigned name; no Microsoft name or MITRE group ID is known to this record. A secondary vendor profile (Brandefense) extends the cluster to Poland and Romania and to CVE-2025-24054, but this is not corroborated by CERT-UA or the primary sources found [S8][S9]. Do not merge facts from that profile with the CERT-UA-attributed 2024 campaign.

attribution.sponsor: Not stated. Reporting describes UAC-0194 only as a threat actor believed to be connected to Russia; no specific Russian service or organization is named in the sources gathered [S2].
attribution.confidence: Attribution to Russia is vendor/press characterization ('believed to be Russian') attached to CERT-UA's UAC-0194 designation; no confidence level was stated in the sources reviewed [S2]. No government attribution to a named service was found.
attribution.basis: CERT-UA associated the URL-file phishing distribution with UAC-0194 after ClearSky shared its findings [S2]. Secondary coverage repeats this; the CERT-UA primary advisory could not be opened [S7].

objectives: A secondary vendor profile characterizes the cluster as focused on credential theft and espionage against government and strategic sectors [S8]. The observed capability (NTLMv2 hash capture enabling pass-the-hash or password recovery, plus a remote access tool) is consistent with credential access and persistent access [S3][S5]. Treat the espionage characterization as unverified beyond that single vendor profile [S8].

sectors: Ukrainian organizations; recipients lured with an academic-certificate theme (education-themed lure) [S2]
Government and strategic sectors (per secondary vendor profile only) [S8]
regions: Poland and Romania (secondary vendor profile only, uncorroborated) [S8]
targeting.notes: ClearSky described very specific targets receiving spear-phishing sent from a compromised Ukrainian academic or government-linked server [S3][S2]. The sending domain reported by The Hacker News was doc.osvita-kp.gov[.]ua; one summary suggested a link to Kamianets-Podilskyi City Council, but another summary of the same coverage said no source confirmed that, so treat it as unverified [S2].

capabilities.summary: Zero-day exploitation of CVE-2024-43451, an NTLMv2 hash disclosure spoofing flaw (CVSS 6.5) triggered by selecting, right-clicking, deleting or dragging a crafted .URL file, patched in Microsoft's November 2024 Patch Tuesday and added to the CISA KEV catalog with a 3 December 2024 remediation date [S3][S5]. Delivery used spear-phishing with a link to a ZIP archive containing the .URL file; the file connected to a remote server to download further payloads, including SparkRAT, and attempted NTLM hash exfiltration over SMB [S2][S3][S2]. Use of a compromised legitimate Ukrainian server as phishing infrastructure indicates tradecraft to improve email credibility [S3]. Earlier ClearSky reporting also associated the lure with CVE-2023-32046 and CVE-2023-36025 targeting [S5].

campaigns.name: Earliest observed CVE-2024-43451 exploitation
campaigns.summary: ClearSky reports exploitation of the NTLM flaw in the wild since at least April 2024, via spear-phishing from a compromised Ukrainian academic server to specific targets.

campaigns.name: Academic-certificate lure with .URL zero-day
campaigns.summary: Phishing urged recipients to renew academic certificates via a link to a ZIP containing a .URL file; the file triggered CVE-2024-43451, fetched SparkRAT and attempted NTLM hash capture over SMB. CERT-UA attributed the distribution to UAC-0194.

campaigns.name: Microsoft patch and KEV listing
campaigns.summary: Microsoft fixed CVE-2024-43451 in November 2024 Patch Tuesday while exploitation was ongoing; CISA added it to the KEV catalog, remediation due 2024-12-03.

campaigns.name: NTLM CVE-2025-24054 campaign against Poland and Romania (not firmly attributed)
campaigns.summary: Check Point observed .library-ms NTLM-harvesting attacks from about 19-21 March 2025 against Polish and Romanian institutions. A secondary vendor profile lists this CVE under UAC-0194, but no CERT-UA statement tying that campaign to UAC-0194 was found.

diamond.adversary: Russia-linked cluster tracked by CERT-UA as UAC-0194; no service or sponsor named [S2].
diamond.capability: CVE-2024-43451 .URL zero-day, NTLMv2 hash capture over SMB, SparkRAT as follow-on payload, ZIP-delivered shortcut files [S2][S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised Ukrainian academic or government-linked mail/web server used to send phishing and host the download; reported domain doc.osvita-kp.gov[.]ua; remote SMB and payload servers [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Ukrainian organizations receiving education-themed lures; Poland and Romania per an uncorroborated vendor profile [S2][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Targeting of Ukraine occurs during the Russia-Ukraine war; the specific tasking requirement is not stated in sources. Espionage motive is a single-vendor characterization [S8].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints with unpatched CVE-2024-43451 (all supported Windows versions affected), NTLM authentication and outbound SMB to untrusted hosts, and email links to ZIP archives [S3].

gaps: The CERT-UA advisory on UAC-0194 could not be opened (fetch failure); all details come from secondary coverage and search summaries [S2].
No Russian service, sponsor or confidence level is stated for UAC-0194 in sources reviewed.
Whether Kamianets-Podilskyi City Council infrastructure was used is inconsistent across summaries and unverified [S2].
Link between UAC-0194 and the 2025 CVE-2025-24054 Poland/Romania activity rests on one secondary vendor profile and is uncorroborated [S8][S9].
Overlap with other CERT-UA or vendor clusters using NTLM-theft and SparkRAT is not established; no vendor aliases or Microsoft name found.
Victim counts, post-compromise actions, data stolen, and activity after November 2024 attributable to UAC-0194 are not public in sources gathered.
Specific IOCs (hashes, IPs) were not reviewed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Windows endpoints and mail gateways in mission-partner and host-nation networks, and NTLM-authenticated file-sharing paths, are key terrain because the chain needs only a shortcut file interaction to leak credentials [S3]. STEP 2: The actor weaponized a zero-day and abused compromised legitimate government or academic mail infrastructure, so sender reputation alone is a weak filter [S3]. STEP 3: The observed template is spear-phishing link, ZIP with .URL, outbound SMB for NTLM hash capture, then SparkRAT [S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is repeated NTLM-theft phishing against Ukrainian and allied government and education contacts using newly disclosed Windows file-handling flaws. MDCOA (analyst inference, not sourced) is use of captured hashes to relay into higher-value networks of coalition partners. Candidate indicators: outbound SMB (TCP 445) to external hosts, .URL files inside archives from email links, SparkRAT process or network artifacts, and emails from legitimate-but-compromised .gov.ua or education domains [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track CISA KEV entries and Windows Patch Tuesday zero-days relevant to NTLM and shortcut handling, since exploitation preceded the patch by months [S3]. (2) Authorities: egress blocking of SMB and NTLM restrictions are configuration actions that need network owner approval across enclaves; coordinate in advance. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize patching and NTLM hardening on systems supporting coalition and Ukraine-related coordination mail. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partners and CERT-UA-equivalent counterparts, noting that attribution beyond 'believed Russian' is not established [S2].
